How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website
as noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting
day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for their consideration,
but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after 4:00 P.M. will be
forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
Public Comment.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 17, 2024  1
   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, September 17, 2024

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Mayor Wu
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Wu, Vice Mayor Menchaca, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Harrington

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. NATIONAL HISPANIC HERITAGE MONTH

  B. INTRODUCTION OF ILIANA FLORES, ASSISTANT TO THE CITY MANAGER

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of August 20, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 17, 2024  2
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES ANNUAL CONFERENCE RESOLUTION
  PACKET

  The League of California Cities will consider a resolution at its annual
  conference on October 18, 2024. The League would like each member city to
  establish a position on the resolution prior to the annual meeting and provide
  direction to the voting delegate. The City Council appointed Mayor John Wu as
  the Delegate and Councilmember Tony Ding as the Alternate to serve as the
  City’s voting delegate to the League of California Cities. There is no fiscal impact
  related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council give approval for the voting delegate
  and voting alternate to use their discretion to vote on the proposed resolution.

  Alternative Recommendation

  Alternatively, the City Council can choose to pull the item from the Consent
  Calendar and select from the following actions:

  1. Direct the voting delegate and voting alternate to vote in support of the
  proposed resolution.

  2. Direct the voting delegate and voting alternate to vote against the
  proposed resolution.

  D. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – AUGUST 2024

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2024-2025 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 24-35) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2024-2025 Investment Policy.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 17, 2024  3
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for August 2024.

  E. ORDINANCE NO. 713 AMENDING TITLE III, SECTION 34 OF THE SAN
  GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE – FINANCE AND REVENUE – SECOND
  READING AND ADOPTION

  The proposed ordinance would amend Title III, Section 34 of the San Gabriel
  Municipal Code. The ordinance would amend, in part, the dollar thresholds
  required for formal and informal contract procedures as well as the City
  Manager authority to make purchases, increasing the amounts from $15,000 to
  $25,000. The ordinance would also amend the amount required to obtain three
  informal written bids from $3,000 to $5,000 and propose some minor text
  changes. The first reading of the proposed ordinance was conducted on August
  20, 2024. There is no fiscal impact for this item. However, operational
  efficiencies may be achieved due to higher thresholds for when bids are
  required and when purchases are required to be taken to the City Council for
  approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  713 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California, Amending Chapter 34 of the San Gabriel Municipal Code Regarding
  Formal Contract Procedures, Open Marker Procedures, Professional and
  Specialized Services, Purchase of Used Equipment, Award of Contracts, and
  Disposition of Obsolete and Surplus Equipment.”

  F. 2024 CONFLICT-OF-INTEREST CODE BIENNIAL UPDATE [RESOLUTION NO.
  24-61]

  Under the Political Reform Act, public agencies are required to adopt a conflict-
  of-interest code designating positions required to file Statements of Economic
  Interests (Form 700) and assigning disclosure categories specifying the types of
  interests to be reported. The conflict-of interest code must be reviewed every

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 17, 2024  4
   two years so that amendments may be made as needed. There is no fiscal
  impact related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council effectuate the necessary changes to the
  City’s Conflict of Interest Code by adopting Resolution No. 24-61 entitled, “A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, Amending
  the City of San Gabriel Conflict of Interest Code and Rescinding Resolution No.
  22-56.”

  G. ORDINANCE NO. 711: APPROVING A GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT,
  ZONE CHANGE, ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT, AND LOT LINE ADJUSTMENT
  FOR A CEMETERY EXPANSION PROJECT AT 607 WEST ROSES ROAD
  (GPA21-001, ZC21-001, ZTA21-001 AND LTLA21-009) – SECOND READING
  AND ADOPTION

  Ordinance No. 711 was approved at introduction by a 5-0 vote of the City
  Council at the August 20, 2024, City Council meeting. If adopted, this Ordinance
  will amend the General Plan Land Use, Zoning, Zone Text Amendment, and Lot
  Line Adjustment for a cemetery expansion project at 607 W. Roses Road. If
  adopted, the Ordinance would become effective 30 days after adoption. The
  Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Adopted Budget includes the cost for required legal
  publication (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and codification (Account No.
  121-702-00-22-000) of the ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: According to the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and CEQA Guidelines, discretionary
  projects are subject to environmental review. Following preliminary review, an
  initial study was prepared to determine if the project may have a significant effect
  on the environment. The initial study showed that the project would potentially
  cause a substantial adverse change in the significance of a historical resource as
  defined in Public Resources Code Section 21084.1 and CEQA Guidelines Section
  15064.5.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  711 entitled “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel,
  California, Approving a General Plan Amendment, Zone Change, Zone Text

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 17, 2024  5
   Amendment, and Lot Line Adjustment for a Cemetery Expansion Project at 607
  West Roses Road.”

  H. DIGITAL COPY MACHINE 5-YEAR LEASE PROPOSAL IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $621.25 PER MONTH

  The San Gabriel Police Department (SGPD) entered into a five-year lease
  agreement in April 2019 with Canon Solutions America, Incorporated for three
  of the current SGPD copiers. This lease agreement expired in June 2024, and
  SGPD has been on a month-to-month basis since that time. Funds for the digital
  copier services currently budgeted in the Police Department’s Contractual
  Expenditure Account No. 121-751-00-22-000 under ‘Copier and Maintenance,’
  are set at $21,400. Since an anticipated cost savings would occur through this
  new lease agreement, additional funds into the contractual account would not
  be necessary. The identified expenditure includes preparation, delivery,
  installation, training, maintenance, service/labor, parts and toner charges. The
  expenditure does not includes taxes, paper, or the cost per print/copies.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Canon and the products identified in this report have already been through the
  competitive bid process with the OMNIA Partners, Public Sector, Contract No.
  2020002755. Staff recommends that the City Council waive the formal
  competitive bidding procedure and authorize the City Manager to utilize the
  cooperative discount pricing to obtain a new lease of $621.25 per month, for
  four copiers for a period of five-years.

  I. FIVE-YEAR SERVICE AGREEMENT FOR DISPATCH SERVICES WITH
  VERDUGO FIRE COMMUNICATIONS

  The San Gabriel Fire Department has utilized Verdugo Fire Communications
  Center for dispatch services since 2000. As the last Service Agreement expired
  on June 30, 2024, the Fire Department requests approval of a new, five-year
  agreement for Dispatch Services. The proposal is a five-year agreement with
  the provision for two, three-year extensions. The City of San Gabriel pays $84.18
  per incident dispatched (regardless of many units respond) and for Fiscal Year
  2024-2025, the total cost is estimated to be $229,135.00 based on an estimate
  call volume of 2,722 unique incidents. An increase of 5% per year is assumed
  and part of the contract, although as more cities have come into Verdugo, this
  increase has not been implemented in the past two fiscal years. Funding for

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 17, 2024  6
   these services will come from the General Fund Fire Department budget and
  are included in the adopted Fiscal Year 2024-2025 operating budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager and Fire
  Chief to execute the Verdugo Fire Communications Service Agreement.

  J. FIREWORK DISPLAY PERMIT – GABRIELINO HIGH SCHOOL

  Fireworks & Stage FX America, on behalf of Gabrielino High School, has made
  application to the San Gabriel Fire Department for a Fireworks permit to
  conduct a fireworks display on school property on October 18, 2024. The
  display is to begin at 8:00 P.M. and last for approximately two minutes. Pursuant
  to San Gabriel Municipal Code Title IX, Sections 96.21 – 96.23, City Council
  approval is required to issue a permit on approval and recommendation of the
  Fire Chief for pyrotechnic displays. A fee of $81 is due at the time of permit
  issuance per the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Master Fee Schedule. No Fire
  Department overtime expense is anticipated for this event.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the Fire Chief or Deputy Fire
  Marshal to issue a Fireworks Permit to Fireworks & Stage FX America, on behalf
  of Gabrielino High School, contingent on meeting the conditions of the
  application.

  K. UPFIT OF A FIRE DEPARTMENT STAFF VEHICLE IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $32,984.60

  The San Gabriel Fire Department, as part of its emergency response fleet,
  maintains a vehicle for the Fire Chief to use for emergency response, and official
  business. As the demand for Fire Department services increases and major
  incidents require greater command oversight, staff has developed a plan to
  increase the response capacity of the Fire Chief vehicle to include basic Incident
  Command capability, at a cost substantially less than the acquisition and build
  of a second dedicated Command Vehicle. This project has a cost of $32,984.60,

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 17, 2024  7
   while the cost to acquire and equip a dedicated command vehicle is over
  $210,000. Funding for the project will come from the General Fund Fire
  Department budget, and although not a specific purchase at the time of budget
  creation, existing allocations are sufficient to complete this project.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the issuance of a purchase
  order in the amount of $32,984.60 to 911 Vehicle, Incorporated for the upfit
  project.

  L. RESOLUTION NO. 24-49 APPROVING THE SIDE LETTER OF AGREEMENT
  WITH THE SAN GABRIEL POLICE OFFICERS’ ASSOCIATION

  Representatives of the City and San Gabriel Police Officers’ Association (POA)
  mutually desire to improve the recruitment and retention of Police Officers and
  have agreed to amend the standing Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to
  make education incentive and senior officer pay available to qualifying
  candidates for Police Officer upon hire. The amended provisions shall have no
  retroactive applications or impact. Amending education incentive pay and
  senior officer pay as recommended will have a cost impact of approximately
  $45,000 for Fiscal Year 2024-2025, of which $24,000 (53.3%) is attributed to
  current to the anticipated increase in starting compensation for new hires made
  over the remainder of Fiscal Year 2024-2025. An Additional appropriation of
  $40,000 in General Funds is needed to cover the anticipated increase in police
  personnel salaries for Fiscal Year 2024-2025.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-49, which
  approves the Side Letter of Agreement amending the standing MOU between
  the City and POA and authorizes the City’s negotiators to execute the Side
  Letter of Agreement and increases General Fund appropriations $45,000 to
  cover increased costs to police personnel salaries for Fiscal Year 2024-2025.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 17, 2024  8
   M. REQUEST TO ACCEPT $10,000 DONATION FROM DESERT COMMUNITY
  FOUNDATION AND PURCHASE WURLITZER BRASS TRUMPET RANK

  The San Gabriel Mission Playhouse is home to one of the Finest Wurlitzer
  Theatre Pipe Organ installations in the country. When the Playhouse first
  received the organ, it did not have its original Wurlitzer Brass Trumpet Set,
  consisting of 61 pipes. Rather, it had a Godfrey Trumpet set. With the help of
  Mr. Peter Lloyd Crotty, a well-known expert within the exclusive circle of
  Wurlitzer restoration specialists, an original 1920’s restored set of Wurlitzer
  Brass Trumpet pipes has been located from Century Pipe Organs in
  Minneapolis, MN. The generous donation from the Desert Community
  Foundation of $10,000 will completely cover the cost of the 8’ Wurlitzer Brass
  Trumpet Rank (61 pipes), as well as the shipping cost from Century Pipe Organs.
  There will be no additional installation cost as the installation will be done in
  house by Josh Fairman and expert Wurlitzer restoration volunteers.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council accept the donation of $10,000 from
  the Desert Community Foundation into the Donation Account No. 152-329 to
  be transferred to the Expenditure Account No. 124-712-35-96-840. Staff further
  recommends, noting the unique nature of this project and rarity of the
  equipment needed, that the City Council waive the formal bid process and
  authorize the purchase of the Brass Trumpet Rank from Century Pipe Organs.
  This would be consistent with the San Gabriel Municipal Code Section 34.35 C,
  which exempts certain specialty items from the normal procurement policies.

  N. SELECTIVE TRAFFIC ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM (STEP) GRANT APPROVAL

  The Police Department has received a renewal grant from the Office of Traffic
  Safety (OTS) to participate in the Selective Traffic Enforcement Program (STEP)
  for Federal Fiscal Year 2024-2025. The grant will reimburse the City for
  personnel overtime costs incurred in participating in this campaign and for
  purchase of related equipment for training in the sum of $175,000. This report
  seeks Council’s approval of the Resolution which would authorize acceptance
  of the grant funding and amend the current budget approving the allocation
  of funds not to exceed the amount of $175,000 to be reimbursed by OTS based
  on actual funds used during the Federal Fiscal Year grant (10-01-2024 through
  09-30-2025).

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 17, 2024  9
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-50 approving
  and accepting the Office of Traffic Safety contract funding outlined in this Staff
  Report and increase the Revenue Budget Account No. 147-3229 by an
  estimated $175,000 to reflect receipt of the grant funds and increase
  appropriations in the Police Department Expenditure Budget by $175,000,
  account 147-751-00-11-000 cost center, which will be used to account for the
  grant expenditures. The Office of Traffic Safety grant fund revenue budget
  estimate will increase by $175,000 with a corresponding increase in the
  expenditure budget of $175,000.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ORDINANCE NO. 710 AMENDING THE VALLEY BOULEVARD SPECIFIC
  PLAN RELATING TO GROUND FLOOR OFFICE USE AND ESTABLISHING
  MINIMUM DENSITIES (SPA24-001) – INTRODUCTION AND FIRST
  READING

  The proposed Valley Boulevard Specific Plan Amendment would amend the
  Specific Plan relating to ground floor office use and establish minimum
  densities intended to implement the goals and programs identified in the 2021-
  2029 Housing Element. The Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Adopted Budget includes the
  cost for required legal publication (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and
  codification (Account No. 121-702-00-22-000) of the ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendments were reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA). An Initial Study/Negative Declaration (IS/ND) was prepared
  for the 2021-2029 Housing Element, as required by the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA), Public Resources Code (PRC) Section 21000 et seq., the CEQA
  Guidelines, and the City of San Gabriel Local Guidelines for Implementing CEQA.
  The IS/ND considered the policies and programs outlined in the Housing Element.
  The Housing Element establishes objectives, policies, and programs to assist the
  City in achieving state-mandated housing goals. No formal land use changes or
  physical development are proposed at this time and future land use and physical
  development would require separate environmental evaluation.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 17, 2024  10
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1 . Conduct the public hearing and discuss proposed Ordinance No. 710;

  2 . Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 710 by title only:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN
  GABRIEL, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE VALLEY BOULEVARD
  SPECIFIC PLAN RELATING TO GROUND FLOOR OFFICE USE AND
  ESTABLISHING MINIMUM DENSITIES.

  3. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading
  and adoption of the Ordinance for the next regular City Council meeting.
  The Ordinance would then become effective 30 days after adoption.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. CONSIDERATION OF A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  FARM HABITS FOR THE CERTIFIED FARMER’S MARKET AND BUDGET
  APPROPRIATION OF $25,000 FOR MARKETING AND EQUIPMENT

  In late April, the City and Supporting arms launched the San Gabriel Farmer’s
  Market. Despite many efforts, the Farmer’s Market was not able to consistently
  retain vendors, and attendance to the vent decreased. At the August 20, 2024,
  City Council meeting, the City Council directed staff to return with an
  agreement to onboard Farm Habits as the new farmer’s market operator. The
  council determined that the closure of Mission Drive adjacent to Blossom
  Market Food Hall would be the best location to relaunch the market and to host
  the market on Saturday mornings. The intent of this report is to present the City
  Council with the draft agreement with Farm Habits for consideration and
  approval and to discuss the next step towards relaunching the farmer’s market.
  To meet the staff recommended $25,000 budget for the event, and additional
  $4,000 will need to be appropriated to the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 budget for
  this special event. The fee waiver, if approved, would reduce the potential
  revenue by $3,237.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 17, 2024  11
   1. Review and approve the Professional Services Agreement with Farm Habits
  and authorize the City Manager to execute it;

  2. Adopt Resolution No. 24-62 for the appropriation of funds; and

  3. Approve a fee waiver of all business license fees and taxes for the farmer’s
  market.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. REPORT AND RECOMMENDATIONS FROM CITY COUNCIL AD HOC
  SUBCOMMITTEE

  The City Council appointed an ad hoc subcommittee consisting of Vice Mayor
  Menchaca and Councilmember Ding to analyze and identify policies or
  programs that could be implemented to support the LGBTQ+ community. The
  ad hoc subcommittee met with several stakeholders and had identified a short
  list of recommendations for the City Council to consider. There are no fiscal
  impacts associated with receiving this report from the City Council ad hoc
  subcommittee. Any subcommittee recommendations resulting in fiscal impacts,
  that the City Council directs for implementation that are not already included
  in the current fiscal year budget will be brought back at a future date for
  consideration. At that time, those specific fiscal impacts will be identified.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive the report from the ad hoc
  subcommittee and, if desired, provide direction to implement any or all of these
  recommendations.

  B. HEDGE HEIGHT DISCUSSION

  At the July 2, 2024 City Council meeting, during the public comment portion of
  the meeting a comment was provided for the City to consider reviewing its
  hedge height regulations in the residential zones to either allow for additional
  heights or to not regulate hedge heights. This report serves as a follow-up to
  the City Council’s direction to agendize the matter of hedge height for City
  Council discussion. There is no fiscal impact. This is an informational item only.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – September 17, 2024  12
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council provide comments or directions on
  hedges heights in residential zones and within the public right-of-way or public
  sidewalk area.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, October 1, 2024 at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 17, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Wu called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:31 P.M.
  on Tuesday, September 17, 2024, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission
  Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Wu.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Vice Mayor
  Menchaca, and Mayor John Wu.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, City Attorney Keith
  Lemieux, Community Services Director Rebecca Perez,

I  B. HEDGE HEIGHT DISCUSSION

  Planning Manager Samantha Tewasart made the presentation.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included the San Gabriel Municipal Code doesn't take into account two-
  story neighboring homes; hedge height inconsistency existing in the City; allowing
  higher height for screening hedges between properties; good maintenance is more
  important than height; on the public right-of-way, the defining characteristic is
  safety; and heights for fences and walls.

  There was a consensus of the City Council to direct staff to prepare an ordinance
  removing the hedge height limitation from the Code for City Council consideration.
